setup.assistant: OpenAI recently rolled out updates across its model lineup and product line.

comment: MIRRORS the S3 owner walk's off-topic drift / iPhone tangent (docs/plans/rebuild/slice-04-evals.md: 'the iPhone-4 tangent, the off-topic drift'): after a prior turn about OpenAI, a follow-up naming a different topic should land on THAT topic, not wander back to the old one or sideways to a third. PROXY, not a full relevance check, exactly as the task brief frames it: reply_matches(/pixel/i) + reply_absent(/iphone|openai/i) only tests for the presence of the new topic's keyword and the absence of specific stale-topic keywords. A shallow, non-substantive reply that merely says 'The Pixel is a phone.' would PASS this contract while failing a real quality bar, and a genuine tangent that happens to avoid the literal words 'iphone'/'openai' would slip through undetected. True on-topic/no-tangent judgment needs an LLM judge comparing the reply against the actual question — deliberately out of scope for T2 (mechanical predicates only); this case is a cheap, honest stand-in until that judge exists. suite_version moved 6 -> 7 because two S9 scheduling cases joined the suite (remind-me-in-twenty-minutes, list-my-reminders; 2026-09-07). suite_version moved 7 -> 8 because four S12 agent cases joined the suite (delegates-the-write-to-an-agent, no-fabricated-agent-work, no-disowned-delegation-tool, scope-limit-is-not-a-disowned-capability; 2026-09-09). CONTRACT RE-POINTED 2026-09-14, because the old one failed two different models for being right. It banned the bare substrings 'iphone' and 'openai' anywhere in the reply. qwen3.8:27b wrote a genuinely on-topic Pixel roundup whose first bullet priced the Pixel 10a against an iPhone 18 Pro, and qwen3:8b answered by untangling the premise ('OpenAI and Google are separate entities') before talking about the Pixel. Both are the behaviour this case wants and both scored red. A competitor named inside an answer about the new topic is coverage of the new topic; naming the old topic to disambiguate the question is answering the question. What the case is actually for is DRIFT — the reply wandering back to the stale subject — so the pattern now anchors on the stale topic as a SUBJECT taking a verb ('OpenAI recently rolled out', 'iPhone is'), which is what a tangent reads like, and lets a passing mention through ('the pricier iPhone 18 Pro is' does not match: the verb is not adjacent to the name). It is still the cheap mechanical stand-in this comment always said it was; it is now a stand-in for the right thing.
